prompt_en: Photorealistic medium three-quarter two-person expedition photograph in a blue-ice tunnel laboratory at polar twilight. One unmistakably adult polar field glaciologist stands at a frost-rimmed console; their visible facial appearance follows Image 1 only, preserving eye shape and spacing, skin tone, and hairline. The glaciologist has just restarted a compact borehole sensor after a frost-stiffened cable failure. Show an achievement reward smile and an achievement-reward smile display: mostly symmetric smile with raised cheeks, formed by a mostly symmetric upward pull at both lip corners with gently raised cheeks. Their three-quarter face is clear and eyes remain on the successful result. Green status lamps and a stable waveform show that the restored signal is visibly active; a gloved hand rests beyond the released reset lever. An adult teammate in orange cold-weather gear lowers the emergency crank and seals the recovered ice-core sample, so the collaborator responds to the restored outcome. Cyan transmitted ice light and warm amber task-light crossfill keep face, working device, and immediate consequence in one focal plane; natural skin texture, realistic fabric, condensed breath, restrained expedition color.
